title: Moses When Harriet Tubman Led Her People to Freedom
fulltitle: Moses When Harriet Tubman Led Her People to Freedom
description:
Harriet Tubman is certainly a national hero. One of my favorite lines in the story: "Lord, make me strong. Help me fight" is juxtaposed with an image of her huddling in a potato hole. I see this an emblematic of all who have SURVIVED- slavery, war, genocide, displacement, all sorts of abuse. They tell the story with their bodies those who did not. While seemingly passive, to fight, to hold on, to never give up is very much an active pursuit. Harriet Tubman had an iron will rooted in her faith and despite overwhelming power against her, she left us an example of what it means to be a true patriot. 
If you'd like to learn more, visit the Harriet Tubman National Underground Railroad National Historical Park on the Eastern Shore of Maryland https://www.nps.gov/hatu/index.htm
...or her home and resting place in Auburn, New York
https://www.harriettubmanhome.com/
The story has songs from Fannie Lou Hamer's album "Songs My Mother Taught Me."
https://folkways.si.edu/fannie-lou-hamer/songs-my-mother-taught-me/african-american-gospel-struggle-protest/music/album/smithsonian
"Keep Your Lamps Trimmed and Burning" bookends the story because I feel Ms. Tubman was, in addition to everything else, an exemplar of this Gospel story. She WAS ready for the "day of the Lord" (AKA the end of the world) and put that into practice. When you suffer such unimaginable cruelty and oppression, you long for such a day, a day of woe for the oppressors but a day of rejoicing for the oppressed. "Therefore, stay awake, for you know neither the day nor the hour." Matthew 25:13.

title: The Stranger by Chris Van Allsburg
fulltitle: The Stranger by Chris Van Allsburg
description:
Of all the seasons, fall is one of my faves. Not to knock the glory of winter or the expectancy of spring, or summer's variety show on Earth and sky, fall marks a slowing down, a return, a time to remember. The days begin to shorten and plant life takes on a different hue and habit, we return to school (in person!) and daily routines, and memories of the past reveal themselves. In the case of our Jewish sisters and brothers who celebrate Sukkot, their memory goes way back! The smell of raked leaves, warm kitchens, carved pumpkin, and apple cider all take me back. Back to my childhood but also my more recent childhood, lived out with my kids and family. I always enjoy Chris Van Allsburg's books and this is no exception. I hope you find it as comforting as I do. Perhaps it will help you to slow down and remember as well.

If you feel so inclined, please consider supporting my work here: patreon.com/TheLateHeavy

title: Zork I Walkthrough with Sound Effects
fulltitle: Zork I Walkthrough with Sound Effects
description:
The story behind this latest (and longest) project is itself worthy of a separate video, LOL. Indeed, modern Youtubers make videos of their own videos in a cycle of self-aggrandizement to further stake out their “brand,” an ironic way to establish your individuality by doing what everyone else is doing. One common Youtube ploy to add subscribers is watching others play video games, as if the actual playing of video games was too boring or difficult; in most cases, the answer is “YES” to both! It’s hard to believe there was a time when video games were very popular WITHOUT cinematic graphics with fast refresh rates. Graphics back then were so rudimentary that game designers, I believe, relied on players to use their imaginations to fill in the blanks or make up for the heavily pixelated figures scrolling on screen. It was great! And, believe it or not, there were games that didn’t use any graphics at all: the text adventure. Also known as interactive fiction, or IF, the gaming interface with the user matches her interaction with it: text in, text out. There is therefore an inherent equality in these games that the more popular graphics-heavy games lack. You’re at the same level as the computer you’re playing on where gamer becomes part of the story and gets to choose how it unfolds. How cool is that? 

This project is my rejoinder to the countless video game videos saturating the internet. Follow our heroine, a dark woman of ambiguous racial background, who finds herself before a white house. What to do next? Read, and listen! I’ll bet your imagination is way better than anything Rockstar games can throw at you!

The origin of this video is simple: I wanted to prove to myself I could do it, AND I thought others might enjoy it. If my project doesn’t check those two boxes, what’s the point? Reliving the Zork Trilogy like this (well, this first installment) brought me a lot of comfort and joy, something we all need these days. When I had time, usually early mornings, Lucky our cat and I got into a bit of a routine. It felt cozy and safe to be in that world and I hope you might feel the same. It helped that Lucky liked to perch on my shoulders too! This wasn’t so much an escape but a reminder of how our own world should be. I think we all love Middle Earth for the same reason. I don’t care so much for the violence, but the evil creatures do provide a suitable sinister counterpoint to an otherwise beautifully rendered world, and keep the pressure on our heroine throughout. Will she make it?    

Recording the audio was tricky and you can hear my kids or the cat in the background a few times. It is not perfect, but it’s “good enough” for me. The flubs and mis-matched voice levels are all part of the fun. Who needs perfection when you have your imagination? I respect yours enough that you’ll help fill in the blanks! If enough people like this video, I might continue with Zork II. I understand that game is a bit harder, as you have to die a few times to win, so that second checkbox will play more a role for that project!

I will be honest, I used a walkthrough to get to the end. Nostalgia is always so subjective and inaccurate, and although I enjoyed my ACTUAL play of Zork I in the late 80’s,, I couldn’t get very far. I enjoyed more the ambiance of the world than “winning” and I always couldn’t figure out what to do next. Mazes annoy me. This time I found a solution made by MIT itself (the writers of Zork were all MIT grads). However, as useful as this one is (with color coded commands!) it is incomplete; you don’t actually beat the game at the end. I suspect this was intentional so you’d have to use at least SOME brain cells to finishing it!
https://web.mit.edu/marleigh/www/portfolio/Files/zork/transcript.html

I did figure out the ending from another website though: http://www.eristic.net/games/infocom/zork1.html

Needless to say, although I used these walkthroughs, the actual project was very much like an IF game, trying to figure out what to do next, and in what order. I died many times (never take an open flame into a gas-filled room!) and although a covid mask will dampen your explosive “p’s,” with a sensitive mic you sound like you have a mask on!

Text is literally what makes up the world. The opening of John’s Gospel comes to mind: “In the beginning* was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” John 1:1 🇺🇦

title: Free Derry: The IRA Drug War
fulltitle: Free Derry: The IRA Drug War
description:
Subscribe to VICE News here: http://bit.ly/Subscribe-to-VICE-News

In February 2014, letter bombs were sent to nine British Military recruitment offices over the course of three days. Londonderry postmarks, a coded message sent to a Northern Irish newspaper, and security forces at Downing Street all pointed to the New IRA as the main suspects.
 
Last Summer, VICE News visited Derry and heard from Gary Donnelly - the most prominent dissident republican in Londonderry, accused of leading operations for the Real IRA - that these attacks on Britain were to be expected as part of "strategic attacks on high profile targets," as "it's England that's occupying Ireland." 
 
In 'Free Derry: The IRA Drug War', VICE News investigate how, sixteen years after the Good Friday peace agreement and on the eve of the first major loyalist parade through the city in four years, dissident republican activity in Derry is increasing thanks to the merger of the Real IRA with anti-drugs vigilantes. 

VICE News reporter Alex Miller speaks to members of the Republican Action Against Drugs (RAAD), who formed the coalition with the Real IRA, and meets supporters as young as thirteen who are being armed with petrol bombs to combat criminal gangs and intervening police.
 
For the first time, Paul Stewart, a close friend of slain Dublin Real IRA leader Alan Ryan, speaks on camera about witnessing the murder, as well as sharing insights on Ryan's war against drug dealers.

Miller also interviews the mother of Andrew Smith, a man who she says was murdered by the Real IRA despite no affiliation with drugs related crime, before hearing from a Derry ex-drug dealer who now claims that, if the New IRA didn't fight drugs, "this town would be filled with ecstasy and rat poison and kids would be dying."
 
VICE encounter a city where kneecappings and shootings are rife, walls are branded with anti-UK  slogans, and where a policeman can scarcely walk down the street - according to Gary Donnelly - "without being killed".

In "Free Derry: The IRA Drug War", VICE unmask the farcical veneer of the UK's 'City of Culture' 2013.

description:
In the dramatic conclusion of the Zork trilogy, our heroine travels to the heart of the Great Underground Empire and faces her most formidable challenges yet. This adaptation of the video game takes some (putting it mildly) liberties in an effort to make the story more realistic, streamlined, and with a more cohesive linguistic and atmospheric aesthetic than the original. For example, I’ve modified certain problems, altered the Royal Puzzle and fleshed out the Dungeon Master’s motives. 

The content warning pertains to the heroine’s teleportation to Zork IV (Enchanter) and her clothing situation at the time.

Note on heroine's appearance: Xiomara's story is not unique. As such, she represents millions of immigrants and their plight for a better life. Therefore, her facial features and other characteristics vary throughout the presentation. She is both one and many. It's also my way to justify the limits of the AI image software.

Thanks again to Drew Cook’s “Gold Machine” blog’s in-depth analysis and critique of the Zork universe.

They grow old and even the best of them one day lose the power of flight. Fortunately, this does not happen in an instant. A witch can feel the strength slowly leaving her broom. The sudden bursts of energy that once carried her quickly into the sky become weak. Longer and longer running starts are needed for takeoff. Speedy brooms that in their youth outraed hawks are passed by slow flying geese. When these things happen, a witch knows it's time to put her old broom aside and have a new one made. On very rare occasions, however, a broom can lose its power without warning and fall with its passenger to the earth below, which is just what happened one cold autumn night many years ago. Out of a moonlit sky, a dark cloaked figure came spinning to the ground. The witch along with her tired broom landed beside a small white farmhouse, the home of a lonely widow named Mina Shaw. At daybreak, Widow Shaw discovered the witch lying in her vegetable garden. She was bruised and bloody and couldn't stand up on her own. In spite of her fear, and because she was a kind woman, Mina Shaw helped the witch inside and put her to bed. The witch asked Mina Shaw to draw the curtains, then wrapped herself tightly in her black cape and fell soundly asleep. She lay there perfectly still all day and all evening. Min Shaw was asleep in a chair by the fireplace where embers of a dying fire glowed on the hearth. The witch knelt and took one of the red hot coals in her hand. Outside she made a fire of leaves and twigs, then dropped a strand of her hair into the flame. The fire hissed and crackled, burning with a brilliant blue light. Before long, the witch could see a dark form flying overhead. It was another witch who circled slowly and landed beside the fire. The two women spoke briefly, the first witch gesturing toward the garden where her old broom rested. Then they sat side by side on the second witch's broom and flew off over the treetops. When Mina Shaw woke up, she wasn't surprised to find that her guest had gone. Witches she knew had unusual powers. It didn't surprise her either when she saw that the old broom had been left behind. The widow guessed it had lost its magic. It was an ordinary broom now, just like the one she kept in her kitchen. As she lay in bed listening to the broom sweeping each room over and over, she wondered if it could learn to do other things. In the morning, she led the broom outside and found out that it was a very good student. She needed to show it how to do something only once. Soon, the broom could chop wood and fetch water, feed the chickens, and bring the cow in from the pasture. It could even pick out simple tunes on the piano. Not a week passed before the widow's neighbors, the Spivies, found out about the broom. Their farm was just down the road, the only other place around. It was one of the eight Spivby children who saw the broom first. When the boy told his father, Mr. Spivby, ran straight across the road to the widow's house. "Is it true?" he demanded. The men who saw it seemed to agree it probably was a wicked thing, but their wives pointed out that it was a great help to the widow and could play the piano well, considering that it struck just one note at a time. No one's feelings were as strong as Mr. Spivy's. It's evil and dangerous, he told everyone who would listen. We'll all be sorry if this thing stays among us. As days went by, the broom seemed as innocent and hardworking as ever. Though it had learned how to do many things, sweeping brought it special pleasure. It was, after all, a broom. Finally, it stopped sweeping. The broom turned to the two boys and knocked them both on the head so hard they fell to the ground in tears. The broom hopped off, but the spibby dog ran after it, yapping and biting at its bristles. "Get him!" the boys yelled. The little dog leapt into the air and caught the broom by the handle, but he was not there for long. That evening, Mr. Spivby drove his wagon up to the widow's house. He was not alone. Three men from the neighboring farms were in the wagon along with a long wooden stake and coils of rope. Mr. Spivy knocked loudly. When she opened her door, Mina was frightened by what she saw.
